title: vpc-netweave: deterministic subnet tiling and endpoint fabric module
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Create a reusable Terraform module (vpc-netweave) that provisions a deterministic, multi-AZ VPC topology aimed at private deployments. The module should:
- Allocate subnet tiling deterministically across AZs and service lanes (control/data/ingress) using a stable hash-based allocator so repeated applies produce stable subnet CIDRs.
- Provision optional public and private subnet sets with configurable CIDR math, minimal fragmentation, and explicit override maps.
- Manage IGW and a configurable NAT fleet: support single NAT Gateway per AZ, or a NAT fleet autoscaling pattern (small pool with elastic IP rotation) via a simple interface (nat_mode = [single|per_az|fleet]).
- Create and configure VPC endpoints for S3, ECR, SSM, and CloudWatch Logs with endpoint policies and optional policy templates per environment. Support both gateway and interface endpoints.
- Build route tables per lane or shared based on route_table_mode variable (per_subnet|shared_by_lane). Implement propagation/blackhole detection and safe route replacement patterns using create_before_destroy where appropriate.
- Emit well-structured outputs (subnet_ids_by_lane_and_az, route_table_ids, endpoint_ids, nat_allocation_map) to support downstream modules (k8s, bastion, peering).
- Include tagging standards, mandatory owner, environment and module_version tags, and KMS-key integration option for endpoint S3 buckets where required.
- Support an upgrade-sentinel pattern: module exposes a module_version tag and a boolean safe_recreate toggle. When safe_recreate=true the module attempts create_before_destroy for NAT and endpoint replacement flows and writes a synthetic terraform state marker (via aws_ssm_parameter) so higher-level orchestration can perform canaries and rollbacks.
- Integrate health checks and automated healing hooks: synthetic probe Lambda (in each AZ) that verifies egress via NAT/IGW and connectivity to core VPC endpoints; CloudWatch Metrics and alarms per AZ; an SSM document for automated remediation (recreate NAT in AZ, rotate EIPs, reconcile route table associations).
- Implement a small test harness in examples/ that uses the module to create a 3-AZ VPC, deploy synthetic probe, and exercise failover by simulating NAT removal.
Implementation notes: use current terraform AWS provider patterns, heavy use of for_each maps for deterministic resource naming, avoid random_id where stability is required, prefer cidrsubnet() with explicit prefix lengths, and provide explicit lifecycle blocks for critical resources. Document tradeoffs for per-AZ NAT vs shared egress gateways and provide guidance for cost vs latency.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes variables for subnet_layout, az_list, nat_mode, route_table_mode, enable_endpoints, endpoint_policy_templates and safe_recreate
Deterministic subnet allocation across repeated applies and plan/apply cycles (no CIDR drift in default mode)
Health probes deployed and CloudWatch metrics/alarms created for NAT/endpoint reachability
Upgrade-sentinel flow documented and tested in examples (create_before_destroy flow verified)
Outputs contain structured maps suitable for downstream modules and the example harness consumes those outputs successfully
Module has a documented PRD, internal design doc, and at least one peer review sign-off from infra and security

notes: This module targets private deployments where deterministic networking and safe upgrade behavior are required. Keep interfaces minimal — downstream consumers should not need to know NAT internals. Provide migration notes for customers moving from a single-shared-egress design to per-az nat_mode.
